limits: Only three Raman features rise above the noise in 60-1100 cm-1: 108.9, 123.2 and 142.9 cm-1. The 108.9 line dominates; the other two are weak. Nothing else is resolved from 150 to 1100 cm-1, and the library match uses only these three positions.

The identification is a DFT-reference match (Computational Raman Database), not an experimental match. No curated experimental mode table exists for InSiTe3 or any other top candidate here, so the full expected spectrum (including modes outside the window or weak modes) cannot be checked. The top scores (0.99 to 0.82) are close, and three peaks cannot separate the candidates; I cannot exclude materials outside the library.
The measured window ends at 1099 cm-1 and starts at 60.5 cm-1; modes below 60 cm-1 or above 1100 cm-1 were not measured and cannot be assessed.

Point spacing is 1.18 cm-1, so the 4 cm-1 FWHM lines are sampled by only about 3 to 4 points. Widths and the 123.2 cm-1 position (error 0.35 cm-1) are less reliable than the 108.9 cm-1 position. No instrument resolution was supplied, so no width is corrected for it.

The 123.2 cm-1 band is a weak shoulder next to the dominant 108.9 cm-1 line; it is supported by a dip near 116 cm-1 in the raw data and a clean residual, but its position and identity rest on a small intensity.

Conditions 532 nm, 295 K, backscattering and layer-normal geometry were given, but no substrate was stated and none was detected. Resonance with excitons was not checked against any reference for the candidate, so intensity ratios say nothing about identity here.
Single spectrum without polarization, so no irrep was checked against a polarization series; the irreps come only from the DFT reference labels.
Layer number, strain, doping and defect density cannot be derived from this spectrum: no relation applies to the candidate and no reference in the skill covers it.
The working-folder name contains a material string. I did not use it as evidence; it is not part of the measurement metadata, and the identification rests on the peaks alone.
